director.chapterArc: A high-stakes tactical confrontation where a boy sacrifices his power to save the group, transitioning from desperate planning to violent action and finally to quiet devastation.
director.restraintNote: Maintain Toren's analytical distance even during physical trauma. The horror is in the mechanics of failure (the sag hole) rather than emotional screaming. Rook's silence must feel heavy with exhaustion, not anger.

cues.delivery: Stoic acceptance. The plan is being proposed and accepted.
cues.through: "Say what you want from me," he said at last.

cues.delivery: Tactical desperation. The plan is being formed under pressure.
cues.from: "You already gave it to me. You gave it to me on the Level in front of everybody and you have not taken it back." Toren's hands had gone cold. "Nobody in this group is bait. And you said you'd never decide otherwise without saying it to our faces first."
cues.through: "Every time you ask him, you check. Every time you check, you pull. And the thing you are pulling on is the only thing keeping that animal's attention off an old woman on a boy's back in an open field.
cues.reason: The group's discussion of the impossible odds.

cues.delivery: Physical exhaustion and pain. The group is breaking down.
cues.from: "I can't run, Toren. That's a fact about today and it's been a fact about every day since the beck. I would be the slowest thing on that field by a distance and Wyck would have to choose between me and your grandmother, and I am not going to make him do that on open ground."
cues.through: "Thirteen years ago this morning," she said, "at a bad hour, in bad weather."
cues.reason: The preparation of the escape route.

cues.delivery: Desperate resolve. The decision to act is made in silence.
cues.from: And then Rook, last, on the footing at the east end, with a boy's fresh awl-hole in the strap on his forearm.
cues.through: Then he stopped looking at it, and started walking, and did not let go of it again.
cues.reason: Toren's final preparation before the confrontation.

cues.delivery: Internal anxiety. The counting is a physical burden.
cues.from: He could feel each one. That was the thing Rook had never told him, because Rook could not have known it — at eleven paces on a towpath it had been a flinch you had to hunt for, and at four minutes of holding it steady in an open glasshouse with your life on it, every check landed like a thumb pressed into a bruise.
cues.through: It came in at the south side, between the first and second footings. Toren was three walls north of it, and it could not run at him.
cues.reason: Toren's internal monologue about the 'warmth' and checking.

cues.delivery: Rhythmic precision. The action is a trade of time and space.
cues.reason: The tactical dance between Toren and the Breach.

cues.delivery: Physical exertion and pain. The cost of the action is felt in every sentence.
cues.from: It cannot cut twice. It has spent the weight. To come over that wall after him it has to bring the weight forward. That is the grinding. That is half a second.
cues.through: A gap in a wall is a line.
cues.reason: Toren's physical struggle to repair the wall.

cues.delivery: Rising tension as the trap is set and then fails.
cues.from: It is a thing that makes a straight line stop being straight.
cues.through: The whole back end of it went through the sagged crust to the hocks.
cues.reason: The moment Toren lures the Breach into the sag hole.

cues.delivery: Cold realization of a fatal error. The trap failed because the enemy does not think.
cues.through: He had known it since a lay-by on the Ninety with the light going, when a man who could not close his left hand had said there's a thing everybody does in the middle, and had said it isn't the putting-down, it's the looking, and had said I have tried to teach it four times to four people and it has not worked once.
cues.reason: Toren's understanding that his plan was based on false premises.

cues.delivery: Internal struggle. The decision to use power is a desperate gamble.
cues.from: He had a hook on his left hand and a thing going away north across open ground toward two people he loved, and he needed, in that order and in that instant, to be somewhere else and to still be holding what he was holding.
cues.through: Four hundred yards out on the open field, the Breach stopped in the middle of a run, in a way that nothing with its weight forward had any business stopping, and turned round.
cues.reason: Toren's internal monologue about the 'hole' in his nature.

cues.delivery: Tactical precision under extreme duress. The fear is in the calculation of survival.
cues.from: Toren Voss stood with his back against a gable end and both feet apart and a hook on his arm, and waited, on purpose, for an eight-foot rising cut with nothing whatever between him and it.
cues.through: The cut was on a rising line, and the whole mass of the thing was committed forward into it. Toren Voss got a foot of it, sideways, with his own body going the other way and two struts in the ground.
cues.reason: The final confrontation with the Breach.

cues.delivery: Clinical observation of a supernatural event. The creature's dissolution is described as physical fact.
cues.through: She did not touch the arm. She got her hand flat on his chest, which was where Rook had taught all four of them to put their hands, in a dry canal, a long time ago, and she held it there.
cues.reason: The moment the Breach ceases to exist.

cues.delivery: Protective warmth and absolute stillness. This is a grounding anchor for Toren's panic.
cues.reason: Dessa's physical contact provides the only stability in the scene.

pauses.after: "Every time you ask him, you check. Every time you check, you pull. And the thing you are pulling on is the only thing keeping that animal's attention off an old woman on a boy's back in an open field.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: Rook's instruction that Toren must not count. The plan hinges on this.

pauses.after: He did it without one word.
pauses.reason: Scene turn: Wyck prepares to carry Senna; the weight of the burden is established.

pauses.after: "Thirteen years ago this morning," she said, "at a bad hour, in bad weather."
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: Senna's final words to Toren before he leaves her behind.
Completed thought: Toren's realization that Rook has been waiting for this moment.

pauses.after: He could feel each one. That was the thing Rook had never told him, because Rook could not have known it — at eleven paces on a towpath it had been a flinch you had to hunt for, and at four minutes of holding it steady in an open glasshouse with your life on it, every check landed like a thumb pressed into a bruise.
pauses.reason: Scene turn: The internal struggle of holding power without checking it.

pauses.after: "Hundred and sixty. Toren, it's come round the corner of the orchard. It's on the grass strip on the south side of the range and it has gone along instead of at you." Dessa's voice did not change by one degree. "It's looking for a line."
pauses.reason: Completed thought: Toren realizes the creature is looking for a line.
Scene turn: The tactical shift from running to fighting at close range.

pauses.after: A gap in a wall is a line.
pauses.reason: Completed thought: Toren understands the gap in the wall is a line for the creature.
Isolating the critical realization about the trap.

pauses.after: The whole back end of it went through the sagged crust to the hocks.
pauses.reason: Scene turn: The trap fails; the ground gives way.
Isolating the shout that breaks Toren's trance.

pauses.after: He got a breath. It came in wrong and half of it did not arrive.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: The realization of failure and the creature's escape.

pauses.after: He had a hook on his left hand and a thing going away north across open ground toward two people he loved, and he needed, in that order and in that instant, to be somewhere else and to still be holding what he was holding.
pauses.reason: Scene turn: Toren makes the decision to use both powers simultaneously.
Isolating the critical question Toren asks himself.

pauses.before: And Toren did not let go.
pauses.reason: Emphasis on the crucial action of holding on.
Emphasis on the sound of the creature's collapse.
Emphasis on the physical consequence of the creature's death.

pauses.after: She did not touch the arm. She got her hand flat on his chest, which was where Rook had taught all four of them to put their hands, in a dry canal, a long time ago, and she held it there.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: Toren realizes his power is gone. The silence must feel heavy.
